Can the Government confirm that all clauses normally required under FAR 52.212-5 have been incorporated and identify where offerors may find the complete list of applicable FAR clauses? Government Response: Refer to Amendment 0001. The Government has modified Section I.1 to formally incorporate FAR 52.212-5 by reference, ensuring all mandatory commercial product and service statutes are legally preserved. The specific statutory sub-clauses applicable to this procurement (including equal opportunity, subcontracting enforcement, and supply chain cybersecurity) have been explicitly checked within that framework. The complete framework consists of the standalone provisions in Sections I and L, governed by the reinstated FAR 52.212-5 block. FAR 52.212-3 (Offeror Representations and Certifications) remains replaced by active, electronic vendor records maintained within SAM.gov under standard commercial streamlining procedures. Item 2: Technical & Contra

he Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) framework enacted via Executive Order 14275 (Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement) and governing agency class deviations, FAR 52.212-5 (Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders—Commercial Products and Commercial Services) has been completely deleted from the FAR system and is no longer used in any capacity. Accordingly, the solicitation is amended as follows: 1. Correction to Amendment 0001 Q&A Log (Item 1): Item 1 of the Q&A log released with Amendment 0001 is hereby rescinded in its entirety. Reaffirmation of FAR 52.212-5 Exclusion: FAR 52.212-5 remains completely excluded from this procurement. Only the specific standalone clauses explicitly written and listed in Section I of this solicitation apply.

S. Virgin Islands. This service is also extended to eligible American citizens residing abroad. The contractor shall be responsible for providing RealSAM Dialog licenses and services required to operate the system in production, while meeting all IT information-system security requirements as required by the Library of Congress. NLS administers the program nationally, while direct service to eligible individuals and institutions is the responsibility of cooperating network libraries in the various states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U. S. Virgin Islands. Thi

hall provide the Library with license and technical support. This support shall be provided on an annual basis at a firm-fixed price. This support shall be provided in blocks of 500. This support service must ensure that users with legacy RealSAM Dialog licenses can use the My Talking Books skill in production. The contractor shall provide the Library with a price schedule (Attachment J3 - Pricing Chart.xlsx) for the following scenarios: A. RealSAM Dialog License Support – An annual fee for blocks of 500 perpetual user licenses for the RealSAM dialog engine. This scenario reflects the current state of affairs where the contractor is hosting all required non-GFE services (Auth Proxy, Streaming Servers, Dialog Engine, etc.). B. RealSAM Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host the Auth Proxy service instead of the contractor. C. RealSAM Legacy Dialog License Support with Auth Proxy and Streaming Servers hosted by the Library – same as scenario A, but the Library would host both the Auth Proxy service and Streaming Servers instead of the contractor.
